    Finite control windows in orbit quotients #

    Once residual finiteness has separated distinct subgroup translates of a finite control window, passage to the subgroup-orbit quotient is faithful on that window: its points remain distinct and the quotient creates no new instances of the chosen interaction relation. This is the set-theoretic locality statement used before transporting vertices, arrows, and meshes in the covering argument.

    source
    def MagnitudeConjecture.CoveringSeparation.OrbitQuotientInteracts {G : Type u} [Group G] {X : Type v} [MulAction G X] (N : Subgroup G) (R : X → X → Prop) (x y : MulAction.orbitRel.Quotient (↥N) X) :
    Prop

    Two subgroup-orbits interact when some representatives interact. This definition is representative-free and does not require the relation to be invariant under translating its two variables independently.
